sanskrit: bhūmau tu nidadhuḥ ke cid bhṛgavo dhanam akṣayam daduḥ ke cid dvijātibhyo jñātvā kṣatriyato bhayam
english: Some of the Bhṛgus buried their imperishable wealth in the earth, while others gave it to twice-born men, knowing the danger from the kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: bhṛgavas tu daduḥ ke cit teṣāṃ vittaṃ yathepsitam kṣatriyāṇāṃ tadā tāta kāraṇāntaradarśanāt
english: Yet other Bhṛgus gave those kṣatriyas their wealth as the kṣatriyas desired, O dear one, having seen another motive behind their actions.

sanskrit: tato mahītalaṃ tāta kṣatriyeṇa yadṛcchayā khanatādhigataṃ vittaṃ kena cid bhṛguveśmani tad vittaṃ dadṛśuḥ sarve sametāḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: Then, O dear one, as a certain kṣatriya was digging the ground by chance, the wealth that had been buried in a Bhārgava household was discovered; all the assembled bull-like kṣatriyas saw it.

sanskrit: avamanya tataḥ kopād bhṛgūṃs tāñ śaraṇāgatān nijaghnus te maheṣvāsāḥ sarvāṃs tān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ā garbhād anukṛntantaś ceruś caiva vasuṃdharām
english: Then, overcome with rage and scorning those Bhṛgus who had sought refuge, those mighty bowmen slew them all with sharpened arrows, cutting down even the unborn in the womb, and they roamed across the earth.

sanskrit: tata ucchidyamāneṣu bhṛguṣv evaṃ bhayāt tadā bhṛgupatnyo giriṃ tāta himavantaṃ prapedire
english: Then, as the Bhṛgus were being exterminated in this manner out of fear, O dear one, the wives of the Bhṛgus fled to the Himālaya mountain.

sanskrit: tāsām anyatamā garbhaṃ bhayād dādhāra taijasam ūruṇaikena vāmorūr bhartuḥ kulavivṛddhaye dadṛśur brāhmaṇīṃ tāṃ te dīpyamānāṃ svatejasā
english: Among them, one Brahmin woman, in fear, bore a radiant embryo concealed in her left thigh for the propagation of her husband's lineage; those kṣatriyas saw that Brahmin woman blazing with her own splendor.

sanskrit: atha garbhaḥ sa bhittvoruṃ brāhmaṇyā nirjagāma ha muṣṇan dṛṣṭīḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ madhyāhna iva bhāskaraḥ tataś cakṣurviyuktās te giridurgeṣu babhramuḥ
english: Then that embryo burst through the Brahmin woman's thigh and issued forth, blinding the sight of the kṣatriyas like the midday sun; and those, now deprived of sight, wandered bewildered in the mountain fastnesses.

sanskrit: tatas te moghasaṃkalpā bhayārtāḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ brahmaṇīṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmur dṛṣṭyarthaṃ tām aninditām
english: Then those bull-like kṣatriyas, their plans foiled and stricken with fear, took refuge with that blameless Brahmin woman for the sake of their sight.

sanskrit: ūcuś caināṃ mahābhāgāṃ kṣatriyās te vicetasaḥ jyotiḥprahīṇā duḥkhārtāḥ śāntārciṣa ivāgnayaḥ
english: And those kṣatriyas, bewildered and deprived of light, tormented by suffering like fires with extinguished flames, spoke to that illustrious woman.

sanskrit: bhagavatyāḥ prasādena gacchet kṣatraṃ sacakṣuṣam upāramya ca gacchema sahitāḥ pāpakarmaṇaḥ
english: "By the grace of Your Holiness, may the kṣatriya class regain its sight; and may we, having desisted from our evil deeds, depart together as one."

sanskrit: saputrā tvaṃ prasādaṃ naḥ sarveṣāṃ kartum arhasi punar dṛṣṭipradānena rājñaḥ saṃtrātum arhasi
english: "You, together with your son, should bestow grace on all of us; by restoring sight you should rescue these kings."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇy uvāca nāhaṃ gṛhṇāmi vas tāta dṛṣṭīr nāsti ruṣānvitā ayaṃ tu bhārgavo nūnam ūrujaḥ kupito 'dya vaḥ
english: The Brahmin woman said: "I do not take your sight from you, O dear ones; I am not filled with anger. But this Bhārgava who was born from the thigh is surely angered with you today."

sanskrit: tena cakṣūṃṣi vas tāta nūnaṃ kopān mahātmanā smaratā nihatān bandhūn ādattāni na saṃśayaḥ
english: "By him, that great-souled one, your sight has surely been seized in his rage, as he remembers his kinsmen who were slain — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: garbhān api yadā yūyaṃ bhṛgūṇāṃ ghnata putrakāḥ tadāyam ūruṇā garbho mayā varṣaśataṃ dhṛtaḥ
english: "When you were slaying even the embryos of the Bhṛgus, O sons, it was then that I bore this embryo in my thigh for a hundred years."

sanskrit: ṣaḍaṅgaś cākhilo veda imaṃ garbhastham eva hi viveśa bhṛguvaṃśasya bhūyaḥ priyacikīrṣayā
english: "The entire Veda with its six ancillaries entered this child even while he was still in the womb, desiring to do what is most pleasing to the lineage of Bhṛgu."

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ pitṛvadhān nūnaṃ krodhād vo hantum icchati tejasā yasya divyena cakṣūṃṣi muṣitāni vaḥ
english: "This one now wishes to slay you in his rage over his father's murder; it is by whose divine energy your eyes have been stripped away."

sanskrit: tam imaṃ tāta yācadhvam aurvaṃ mama sutottamam ayaṃ vaḥ praṇipātena tuṣṭo dṛṣṭīr vimokṣyati
english: "Entreat him, O dear ones — Aurva, my most excellent son; pleased by your prostration, he will release your sight."

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca evam uktās tataḥ sarve rājānas te tam ūrujam ūcuḥ prasīdeti tadā prasādaṃ ca cakāra saḥ
english: The Gandharva said: Thus addressed, all those kings then spoke to him who had been born from the thigh, saying "Be pleased," and he thereupon showed them his grace.

sanskrit: anenaiva ca vikhyāto nāmnā lokeṣu sattamaḥ sa aurva iti viprarṣir ūruṃ bhittvā vyajāyata
english: And by this very fact he became renowned by that name throughout the worlds — that best of men, the brahmin seer Aurva, born by bursting through the thigh (ūru).

sanskrit: cakṣūṃṣi pratilabhyātha pratijagmus tato nṛpāḥ bhārgavas tu munir mene sarvalokaparābhavam
english: Having recovered their sight, the kings then departed; but the Bhārgava sage resolved upon the destruction of all the worlds.

sanskrit: sa cakre tāta lokānāṃ vināśāya mahāmanāḥ sarveṣām eva kārtsnyena manaḥ pravaṇam ātmanaḥ
english: That great-minded one, O dear one, turned his mind entirely and utterly toward the destruction of all the worlds.

sanskrit: icchann apacitiṃ kartuṃ bhṛgūṇāṃ bhṛgusattamaḥ sarvalokavināśāya tapasā mahataidhitaḥ
english: That best of the Bhṛgus, wishing to exact retribution for the Bhṛgus, magnified by his great austerities, turned his mind toward the destruction of all the worlds.

sanskrit: tāpayām āsa lokān sa sadevāsuramānuṣān tapasogreṇa mahatā nandayiṣyan pitāmahān
english: He tormented the worlds, including gods, asuras, and humans, with his fierce great austerities, intent on gladdening his ancestral fathers.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ pitaras tāta vijñāya bhṛgusattamam pitṛlokād upāgamya sarva ūcur idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then his ancestral fathers, O dear one, recognizing that best of the Bhṛgus, all came from the world of the ancestors and spoke these words to him.

sanskrit: aurva dṛṣṭaḥ prabhāvas te tapasograsya putraka prasādaṃ kuru lokānāṃ niyaccha krodham ātmanaḥ
english: "Aurva, we have witnessed the power of your fierce austerity, dear son. Show grace to the worlds; restrain your wrath."

sanskrit: nānīśair hi tadā tāta bhṛgubhir bhāvitātmabhiḥ vadho 'bhyupekṣitaḥ sarvaiḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ vihiṃsatām
english: "For at that time, O dear one, the slaughter by those kṣatriyas who were doing violence was deliberately overlooked by all those Bhṛgus of cultivated soul, who were not powerless."

sanskrit: āyuṣā hi prakṛṣṭena yadā naḥ kheda āviśat tadāsmābhir vadhas tāta kṣatriyair īpsitaḥ svayam
english: "For when, having lived to a very great age, weariness entered us, it was then, O dear one, that we ourselves desired to be slain by the kṣatriyas."

sanskrit: nikhātaṃ tad dhi vai vittaṃ kena cid bhṛguveśmani vairāyaiva tadā nyastaṃ kṣatriyān kopayiṣṇubhiḥ kiṃ hi vittena naḥ kāryaṃ svargepsūnāṃ dvijarṣabha
english: "Indeed that wealth buried in a certain Bhārgava household was deposited there precisely in order to create enmity, by those who wished to provoke the kṣatriyas to anger. What use is wealth to us, O best of twice-born, who are longing for heaven?"

sanskrit: yadā tu mṛtyur ādātuṃ na naḥ śaknoti sarvaśaḥ tadāsmābhir ayaṃ dṛṣṭa upāyas tāta saṃmataḥ
english: "But when Death was utterly unable to take us, then this means was seen and approved by us, O dear one."

sanskrit: ātmahā ca pumāṃs tāta na lokāṃl labhate śubhān tato 'smābhiḥ samīkṣyaivaṃ nātmanātmā vināśitaḥ
english: "And a man who kills himself, O dear one, does not attain the auspicious worlds; therefore, having considered this, we did not destroy ourselves by our own hand."

sanskrit: na caitan naḥ priyaṃ tāta yad idaṃ kartum icchasi niyacchedaṃ manaḥ pāpāt sarvalokaparābhavāt
english: "Nor is this pleasing to us, dear one — what you wish to do now. Restrain this mind from the sin of destroying all the worlds."

sanskrit: na hi naḥ kṣatriyāḥ ke cin na lokāḥ sapta putraka dūṣayanti tapas tejaḥ krodham utpatitaṃ jahi
english: "For no kṣatriyas and no seven worlds, O son, can taint our austerities and our splendor. Abandon this wrath that has arisen."

sanskrit: aurva uvāca uktavān asmi yāṃ krodhāt pratijñāṃ pitaras tadā sarvalokavināśāya na sā me vitathā bhavet
english: Aurva said: "The vow I made in my wrath back then, O ancestors, for the destruction of all the worlds — that must not go unfulfilled for me."

sanskrit: vṛthāroṣapratijño hi nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe anistīrṇo hi māṃ roṣo dahed agnir ivāraṇim
english: "For I am not able to live on as one whose wrathful vow goes in vain; the unfulfilled wrath would burn me like fire burns kindling-wood."

sanskrit: yo hi kāraṇataḥ krodhaṃ saṃjātaṃ kṣantum arhati nālaṃ sa manujaḥ samyak trivargaṃ parirakṣitum
english: "The man who endures wrath that has arisen for just cause is not capable of properly protecting the three aims of life."

sanskrit: aśiṣṭānāṃ niyantā hi śiṣṭānāṃ parirakṣatā sthāne roṣaḥ prayuktaḥ syān nṛpaiḥ svargajigīṣubhiḥ
english: "Wrath is justly employed by kings who desire heaven, as a restrainer of the undisciplined and a protector of the disciplined."

sanskrit: aśrauṣam aham ūrustho garbhaśayyāgatas tadā ārāvaṃ mātṛvargasya bhṛgūṇāṃ kṣatriyair vadhe
english: "I heard, lying in the thigh, resting in the womb-bed, the outcry of the company of mothers at the slaughter of the Bhṛgus by the kṣatriyas."

sanskrit: sāmarair hi yadā lokair bhṛgūṇāṃ kṣatriyādhamaiḥ āgarbhotsādanaṃ kṣāntaṃ tadā māṃ manyur āviṣat
english: "When the utter extermination of the Bhṛgus, down to the unborn in the womb, by the lowest of kṣatriyas was endured by the worlds together with the gods, then wrath seized me."

sanskrit: āpūrṇakośāḥ kila me mātaraḥ pitaras tathā bhayāt sarveṣu lokeṣu nādhijagmuḥ parāyaṇam
english: "My mothers and fathers, it seems, overflowing with power, did not find a refuge in any of the worlds out of fear."

sanskrit: tān bhṛgūṇāṃ tadā dārān kaś cin nābhyavapadyata yadā tadā dadhāreyam ūruṇaikena māṃ śubhā
english: "When no one then came to the aid of those wives of the Bhṛgus, it was then that this auspicious one bore me alone in her thigh."

sanskrit: pratiṣeddhā hi pāpasya yadā lokeṣu vidyate tadā sarveṣu lokeṣu pāpakṛn nopapadyate
english: "When a restrainer of evil exists in the worlds, then an evildoer finds no foothold in all the worlds."

sanskrit: yadā tu pratiṣeddhāraṃ pāpo na labhate kva cit tiṣṭhanti bahavo loke tadā pāpeṣu karmasu
english: "But when the evildoer finds no restrainer anywhere, then many in the world persist in evil deeds."

sanskrit: jānann api ca yaḥ pāpaṃ śaktimān na niyacchati īśaḥ san so 'pi tenaiva karmaṇā saṃprayujyate
english: "And he who, though knowing evil and capable, does not restrain it, even though he is the lord — he too becomes implicated in that very deed."

sanskrit: rājabhiś ceśvaraiś caiva yadi vai pitaro mama śaktair na śakitā trātum iṣṭaṃ matveha jīvitam
english: "If my fathers, though able, could not be protected by kings and lords — counting life here as desirable —"

sanskrit: ata eṣām ahaṃ kruddho lokānām īśvaro 'dya san bhavatāṃ tu vaco nāham alaṃ samativartitum
english: "— therefore I am enraged against them; being today the lord of the worlds. Yet your words I am not able to simply transgress."

sanskrit: mama cāpi bhaved etad īśvarasya sato mahat upekṣamāṇasya punar lokānāṃ kilbiṣād bhayam
english: "And for me too, as an existing lord, this would be a great thing — again to have fear of sin from overlooking the worlds."

sanskrit: yaś cāyaṃ manyujo me 'gnir lokān ādātum icchati dahed eṣa ca mām eva nigṛhītaḥ svatejasā
english: "And this fire born of my wrath, which wishes to devour the worlds — if suppressed, it would burn me myself with its own energy."

sanskrit: bhavatāṃ ca vijānāmi sarvalokahitepsutām tasmād vidadhvaṃ yac chreyo lokānāṃ mama ceśvarāḥ
english: "I know your desire for the welfare of all the worlds. Therefore, O lords, ordain what is best for the worlds and for me."

sanskrit: pitara ūcuḥ ya eṣa manyujas te 'gnir lokān ādātum icchati apsu taṃ muñca bhadraṃ te lokā hy apsu pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: The ancestral fathers said: "This fire born of your wrath that wishes to devour the worlds — release it into the waters; good fortune to you, for the worlds are established in water."

sanskrit: āpomayāḥ sarvarasāḥ sarvam āpomayaṃ jagat tasmād apsu vimuñcemaṃ krodhāgniṃ dvijasattama
english: "All flavors are water-born, the entire world is water-born; therefore release this fire of wrath into the waters, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: ayaṃ tiṣṭhatu te vipra yadīcchasi mahodadhau manyujo 'gnir dahann āpo lokā hy āpomayāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: "Let this fire of your wrath remain, O brahmin, in the great ocean if you so wish, burning the waters — for the worlds are declared to be water-born."

sanskrit: evaṃ pratijñā satyeyaṃ tavānagha bhaviṣyati na caiva sāmarā lokā gamiṣyanti parābhavam
english: "Thus this vow of yours will be fulfilled, O sinless one, and the worlds together with the gods will not come to destruction."

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca tatas taṃ krodhajaṃ tāta aurvo 'gniṃ varuṇālaye utsasarja sa caivāpa upayuṅkte mahodadhau
english: Vasiṣṭha said: Then Aurva, O dear one, released that fire born of wrath into the abode of Varuṇa; and that fire indeed uses the waters, dwelling in the great ocean.

sanskrit: mahad dhayaśiro bhūtvā yat tad vedavido viduḥ tam agnim udgiran vaktrāt pibaty āpo mahodadhau
english: Becoming a great horse's head — which those who know the Veda know of — it continually drinks the waters of the great ocean, vomiting forth that fire from its mouth.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam api bhadraṃ te na lokān hantum arhasi parāśara parān dharmāñ jānañ jñānavatāṃ vara
english: "Therefore you too, good fortune to you, should not desire to destroy the worlds, O Parāśara; knowing the highest dharmas, O best among the wise."

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca evam uktaḥ sa viprarṣir vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā nyayacchad ātmanaḥ kopaṃ sarvalokaparābhavāt
english: The Gandharva said: Thus addressed by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, that brahmin seer restrained his own wrath from destroying all the worlds.

sanskrit: īje ca sa mahātejāḥ sarvavedavidāṃ varaḥ ṛṣī rākṣasasatreṇa śākteyo 'tha parāśaraḥ
english: And that son of Śakti, the greatly resplendent Parāśara, best among those who know all the Vedas, performed a rākṣasa-sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato vṛddhāṃś ca bālāṃś ca rākṣasān sa mahāmuniḥ dadāha vitate yajñe śakter vadham anusmaran
english: Then that great sage, remembering the murder of Śakti, burned both aged and young rākṣasas in that extended sacrifice.

sanskrit: na hi taṃ vārayām āsa vasiṣṭho rakṣasāṃ vadhāt dvitīyām asya mā bhāṅkṣaṃ pratijñām iti niścayāt
english: For Vasiṣṭha did not restrain him from the slaughter of the rākṣasas, out of the firm resolve: "I must not break his vow a second time."

sanskrit: trayāṇāṃ pāvakānāṃ sa satre tasmin mahāmuniḥ āsīt purastād dīptānāṃ caturtha iva pāvakaḥ
english: That great sage in that sacrifice stood before the three blazing sacred fires like a fourth fire.

sanskrit: tena yajñena śubhreṇa hūyamānena yuktitaḥ tad vidīpitam ākāśaṃ sūryeṇeva ghanātyaye
english: By that pure sacrifice being offered in the proper manner, the sky was illuminated, like by the sun at the end of the rainy season.

sanskrit: taṃ vasiṣṭhādayaḥ sarve munayas tatra menire tejasā divi dīpyantaṃ dvitīyam iva bhāskaram
english: All the sages there, led by Vasiṣṭha, regarded him, blazing in the sky with his splendor, as a second sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramaduṣprāpam anyair ṛṣir udāradhīḥ samāpipayiṣuḥ satraṃ tam atriḥ samupāgamat
english: Then Atri, that sage of noble intellect, wishing to bring to completion that sacrifice which was supremely difficult for others to complete, approached him.

sanskrit: tathā pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuś caiva mahākratum upājagmur amitraghna rakṣasāṃ jīvitepsayā
english: Likewise Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu also approached that great sacrifice, O slayer of enemies, desiring life for the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: pulastyas tu vadhāt teṣāṃ rakṣasāṃ bharatarṣabha uvācedaṃ vacaḥ pārtha parāśaram ariṃdamam
english: Then Pulastya, O bull of the Bharatas, O Pārtha, spoke these words to Parāśara the tamer of enemies, to stop the slaughter of those rākṣasas.

sanskrit: kaccit tātāpavighnaṃ te kaccin nandasi putraka ajānatām adoṣāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ rakṣasāṃ vadhāt
english: "I hope you are without impediment, dear one; I hope you find joy, O son — not in the slaughter of all these rākṣasas who are ignorant and without fault."

sanskrit: prajocchedam imaṃ mahyaṃ sarvaṃ somapasattama adharmiṣṭhaṃ variṣṭhaḥ san kuruṣe tvaṃ parāśara rājā kalmāṣapādaś ca divam āroḍhum icchati
english: "This total extermination of a lineage, O best among soma-drinkers — you, being among the highest, are doing what is most unrighteous, O Parāśara. And King Kalmāṣapāda now desires to ascend to heaven."

sanskrit: ye ca śaktyavarāḥ putrā vasiṣṭhasya mahāmuneḥ te ca sarve mudā yuktā modante sahitāḥ suraiḥ sarvam etad vasiṣṭhasya viditaṃ vai mahāmune
english: "And those sons of the great sage Vasiṣṭha who were superior to Śakti — they all rejoice with delight, together with the gods. All this is known to Vasiṣṭha, O great sage."

sanskrit: rakṣasāṃ ca samuccheda eṣa tāta tapasvinām nimittabhūtas tvaṃ cātra kratau vāsiṣṭhanandana sa satraṃ muñca bhadraṃ te samāptam idam astu te
english: "And the extermination of these ascetic rākṣasas — you, O son of Vasiṣṭha's joy, have been the instrument of it in this sacrifice. Release this sacrifice; good fortune to you — let this be concluded."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pulastyena vasiṣṭhena ca dhīmatā tadā samāpayām āsa satraṃ śāktiḥ parāśaraḥ
english: Thus addressed by Pulastya and the wise Vasiṣṭha, that son of Śakti, Parāśara, then brought the sacrifice to a close.

sanskrit: sarvarākṣasasatrāya saṃbhṛtaṃ pāvakaṃ muniḥ uttare himavatpārśve utsasarja mahāvane
english: The sage released the fire that had been gathered for the universal rākṣasa-sacrifice on the northern slope of the Himālayas, in the great forest.

sanskrit: sa tatrādyāpi rakṣāṃsi vṛkṣān aśmāna eva ca bhakṣayan dṛśyate vahniḥ sadā parvaṇi parvaṇi
english: That fire is seen there even today, consuming rākṣasas, trees, and very rocks, always at each and every new moon and full moon.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca rājñā kalmāṣapādena gurau brahmavidāṃ vare kāraṇaṃ kiṃ puraskṛtya bhāryā vai saṃniyojitā
english: Arjuna said: "For what reason was the wife appointed to that teacher, the best among knowers of Brahman, by King Kalmāṣapāda?"

sanskrit: jānatā ca paraṃ dharmaṃ lokyaṃ tena mahātmanā agamyāgamanaṃ kasmād vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā kṛtaṃ tena purā sarvaṃ vaktum arhasi pṛcchataḥ
english: "And why did the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, knowing the highest dharma and worldly propriety, approach one who was unapproachable? That great-souled one did so in the past — you should tell me everything, as I ask."

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca dhanaṃjaya nibodhedaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi vasiṣṭhaṃ prati durdharṣaṃ tathāmitrasahaṃ nṛpam
english: The Gandharva said: "Listen to this, O Dhanaṃjaya, that which you ask me about — regarding Vasiṣṭha the invincible and likewise the king who endured his enemies."

sanskrit: kathitaṃ te mayā pūrvaṃ yathā śaptaḥ sa pārthivaḥ śaktinā bharataśreṣṭha vāsiṣṭhena mahātmanā
english: "I have told you earlier, O best of the Bharatas, how that king was cursed by Śakti, the great-souled son of Vasiṣṭha."

sanskrit: sa tu śāpavaśaṃ prāptaḥ krodhaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ nirjagāma purād rājā sahadāraḥ paraṃtapaḥ
english: "But that king, having fallen under the power of the curse, his eyes overwhelmed with fury, departed from the city together with his wife, O scorcher of enemies."

sanskrit: araṇyaṃ nirjanaṃ gatvā sadāraḥ paricakrame nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ nānāsattvasamākulam
english: "Having gone to the uninhabited forest, he wandered together with his wife through it — teeming with many herds of deer, crowded with many creatures."

sanskrit: nānāgulmalatācchannaṃ nānādrumasamāvṛtam araṇyaṃ ghorasaṃnādaṃ śāpagrastaḥ paribhraman
english: "Dense with thickets of various shrubs and vines, covered with various trees, that forest resounding with dreadful sounds — he, seized by the curse, roamed through it."

sanskrit: sa kadā cit kṣudhāviṣṭo mṛgayan bhakṣam ātmanaḥ dadarśa suparikliṣṭaḥ kasmiṃś cid vananirjhare brāhmaṇīṃ brāhmaṇaṃ caiva maithunāyopasaṃgatau
english: "One day, seized with hunger, searching for food for himself, greatly afflicted, he came upon a certain forest stream and saw a Brahmin woman and a Brahmin man who had come together for the purpose of union."
